name: South Korea
summary: South Korea is not in the EU or EEA, so nobody has free movement: EU, US and other citizens all need a visa or status. There is no retiree or passive-income visa. For investors the main routes are the public-interest investment scheme (KRW 1.5 billion for F-2, KRW 3 billion for direct F-5), a regional tourism and leisure real estate scheme (KRW 1 billion, mainly Jeju), and the D-8 corporate visa (from KRW 100 million, for people who run the company). Remote workers can use the F-1-D workation visa (income about 1x to 2x Korean per-capita GNI, stay up to 3 years). Same rules for all three groups.
naturalisation: General naturalisation (Nationality Act art. 5) needs 5 consecutive years of domicile, qualification for permanent residence (F-5), adult status, good conduct, self-support and basic knowledge of Korean language and customs. Shorter periods apply to spouses of Korean nationals and some other groups (art. 6, 7).
dual_citizenship_note: Art. 10(1) of the Nationality Act: a naturalised person with a foreign nationality must renounce it within one year. Art. 10(2) lets certain groups (e.g. some marriage migrants and special-naturalisation cases) instead vow not to exercise the foreign nationality in Korea; failure to comply causes loss of Korean nationality. Exact eligible groups not fully checked.

routes.name: Public-interest investment immigration, general (F-2, then F-5)
routes.summary: Invest at least KRW 1.5 billion in a public-interest fund designated by the Minister of Justice and receive an F-2 residence status with free economic activity. Keeping the investment for five years allows an F-5 permanent residence application.
routes.requirements: Invest at least KRW 1.5 billion in a public-interest fund designated and announced by the Minister of Justice (threshold raised from KRW 500 million on 29 June 2023). The F-2 status carries free economic activity. After five years of keeping the investment the holder can be granted F-5. Funds, minimum holding terms and the list of designated funds are set by Ministry of Justice notices that were not read in full. The retirement variant (KRW 300 million, age 55+) was abolished on the same date.

routes.summary: Invest at least KRW 3 billion in a designated public-interest fund and pledge to keep it for five years, and you are granted F-5 permanent residence at once.

routes.status_note: Regional scheme (Jeju, Incheon Songdo/Yeongjong/Cheongna, Pyeongchang Alpensia, Yeosu Gyeongdo, Busan Haeundae and others). Minimum raised from KRW 500 million to KRW 1 billion in May 2023 and the scheme renamed. The Korea Times (Dec 2023) gave 30 April 2026 as the end date for four regions; Jeju announced in February 2026 that its operating period runs to 31 December 2027. No Ministry of Justice notice confirming the extension was found.
routes.tax_note: A residence permit does not by itself make you tax resident; Korean tax residence turns on domicile or 183 days of residence (not researched here, see the Korea tax file). Property tax and acquisition tax apply to the purchase (not researched).
routes.name: Tourism and leisure facility investment immigration (F-2, then F-5)
routes.summary: Buy a designated tourist resort condominium or accommodation facility for at least KRW 1 billion in a designated area (mainly Jeju) and receive F-2 residence. After five years of keeping the investment you can apply for F-5 permanent residence.
routes.requirements: Investment of at least KRW 1 billion in tourism or resort facilities designated by the Minister of Justice (resort condominiums in tourist zones, general and living accommodation facilities); real estate outside the designation does not qualify. Investment must be maintained for five years for F-5. Whether the scheme is still open in each region on 17 October 2026 is not confirmed by an official notice.

routes.name: Corporate investment visa (D-8)
routes.summary: Invest at least KRW 100 million in a Korean company (registered as foreign-invested) and hold a stake of at least 10 percent to get a D-8 corporate investment visa. It is a working-and-business status, not a route to residence by passive investment.
routes.requirements: Per a consultancy summary: investment of at least KRW 100 million in a Korean corporation remitted from abroad, voting shares of at least 10 percent (or shares together with an executive appointment contract), investment reported at a foreign exchange bank and the company registered as foreign-invested. Initial stay up to 5 years for D-8-1 and D-8-3, up to 2 years for D-8-2 and D-8-4 as decided by the immigration office. Sub-type labels differ between sources. Not checked against the Immigration Act enforcement decree.

routes.name: Workation / digital nomad visa (F-1-D)
routes.summary: Remote workers employed by a foreign company can stay in Korea on an F-1-D visa, now permanent since 30 June 2026, for up to 3 years. Income must reach a multiple of Korean per-capita GNI, lower for young applicants outside the Seoul region.
routes.requirements: Ministry of Justice (press page): programme made permanent from 30 June 2026 after a pilot from 2024, stay up to 3 years, income bar eased for young applicants and those living outside the Seoul metropolitan area. Details per a law-firm summary (not the press release text): age 18+, at least one year working for a foreign employer or owning a foreign company in the same industry, remote work only (no work or profit-making in Korea), health insurance of at least KRW 100 million, income after tax of 1x to 2x previous-year per-capita GNI depending on age and region (about KRW 104.83 million a year, i.e. 2x, for age 35+ in the Seoul region; about KRW 52.41 million for 1x). Initial stay 1 year, renewed annually. Spouse and minor children may accompany. Income figure converted from a GNI multiple; GNI base year sources differ.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Korea; B-1, B-2 or C-3 visitors may change status in-country

routes.name: Employment visa (E-7 and related)
routes.summary: Employment in a Korean organisation needs a sponsored work visa, mainly E-7 for occupations designated by the Minister of Justice. The employer drives the application.
routes.requirements: E-7: activities designated by the Minister of Justice for a person invited by a public or private organisation in Korea (Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act, art. 12). Qualification criteria differ between sources (degree and experience); the list of eligible occupations is maintained by the Ministry. Embassy page states a visa stay of up to 1 year at first.
routes.physical_presence: Work for the sponsoring employer in Korea

open_questions: Public-interest investment: designated funds, minimum holding terms, the physical presence requirement and fees were not found in sources read; the MOJ press release (29 June 2023) gives thresholds only.
Tourism and leisure real estate scheme: no Ministry of Justice notice found confirming the extension to 31 December 2027 (Jeju announcement only) or its status in each region on 17 October 2026.

F-1-D: the MOJ press release text with the exact income multiples by age and region was not readable; the tiers (1x, 1.5x, 2x GNI) and the GNI base (KRW 52.41 million for 2025 in one source, KRW 52.57 million for 2026 on a MOFA page) come from secondary sources and conflict. Whether all nationalities qualify (the pilot had regional embassy lists) was not verified.
D-8: threshold, 10 percent share rule and sub-types come from a consultancy page; the Immigration Act enforcement decree was not read. Government fees not sourced.
F-5 by corporate investment (F-5-5) and general F-5 (2x GNI plus KIIP level 5 per a law-firm summary) were not verified from an official text and are not included as routes.
F-1 visiting family: no official source on eligibility was found, so it is not included as a route.
E-7 occupation list, qualification criteria and fees not sourced from an official page.
Government fees for every route are not sourced (null).
Whether any route gives credit toward the 5-year naturalisation residence period was not researched.
